items.title: Live: Emotional Starmer quits as PM to focus on 'most important job'
items.description: Sir Keir Starmer says he will step down as UK prime minister. Follow live.

items.title: Sir Keir Starmer's landslide win left him with shaky foundations
items.description: The former prosecutor who styled himself as a safe, even boring, pair of hands became the first Labour PM in 14 years to win in a landslide. It was not enough to keep him in the job.

items.title: Starmer succumbs to intense pressure and resigns as UK Labour leader
items.description: Sir Keir Starmer says he will resign as prime minister of the United Kingdom and spend more time as a husband and father.

items.title: Watch Sir Keir Starmer's resignation speech in full
items.description: Sir Keir Starmer has announced his resignation as Britain's Prime Minister.

items.title: The moment Tehran's men leave JD Vance waiting in a Swiss negotiating room
items.description: In a room in a glamorous Swiss resort, the United States delegation, Pakistani and Qatari officials were awaiting the arrival of the Iranian representatives. But as Tehran's men enter the room, they appear to notice the press.

items.title: Second Australian case of deadly bird flu confirmed
items.description: Authorities say a second bird found sick on WA's south coast had the deadly H5 strain of avian flu, as one of the nation's biggest chicken producers announces it is locking down its WA operations.

items.title: What we know about how H5N1 bird flu got here and where it may appear next
items.description: Authorities were worried about avian influenza coming in from the north, until the virus started moving across the Southern Ocean. Now infected birds have been found in Western Australia. Where else could birds carrying the virus land?

items.title: Australian trust in China grows as belief in US hits record low
items.description: The Lowy Institute's latest poll shows Australia's trust in the US has fallen to a record low.

items.title: Australia secures biggest-ever defence export deal with Canada
items.description: Canada is buying a powerful radar system to monitor the Arctic, modelling the system on Australia's JORN radar.

items.title: Victoria ended native forest logging. So where are these trees coming from?
items.description: Four Corners follows the logs, and the money, to uncover how efforts to end logging have shifted the timber trade across state borders.

items.title: Operator of troubled Callide power station sued for more than $1b
items.description: Foreign investment group Sev.en said a series of catastrophic failures at the Callide power station had led to 1,700 days of lost generation capacity.

items.title: Japan to increase entry visa fees by more than five times current amount
items.description: Japan will quintuple entry visa fees starting from July 1, but most Australians will not be affected.

items.title: Quick hits: Iran's incredible keeper and young Yamal starts in style
items.description: Young Lamine Yamal scored less than 10 minutes into his World Cup debut; Iran and Cabo Verde both held out for famous draws against highly-fancied opponents Belgium and Uruguay respectively; and Cabo Verde's most famous mum arrives to see her son. Here's the quick hits from the World Cup.

items.title: Tax system favours older Australians over younger, report finds
items.description: Australia's tax policy settings are leading to vastly different outcomes for people who have the same gross incomes but are simply different ages, a new report shows.

items.title: 2.7 tonnes of cocaine found in elaborate bunker system at Sydney property
items.description: A record 2.7 tonnes of cocaine worth an estimated street value of $816 million has been seized at a semi-rural property in Greater Western Sydney.

items.title: Four of our best winter stew recipes for weeknight dinners
items.description: From a hearty beef and veggie blend to chicken and vegetarian options, these are some of our favourite stew recipes for cosy nights in.

items.title: Hugh Jackman embraces brutality in The Death of Robin Hood
items.description: Plus Toy Story 5 trots out the same old games, Australian horror scores another winner and Colony uses zombies to ring the warning bell about AI.

items.title: Final beanie festival a hit with crowds as $400k worth of caps sold
items.description: The 30th and final Alice Springs Beanie Festival has been a sellout, setting a new record of $400,000 worth of beanies sold in three days.

items.title: Potential students allege visa scam tied to education consultancy
items.description: Aspiring students looking to study abroad in Australia say they've been left blindsided and with their futures in doubt after an education consultancy promised them migration and visa advice.

items.title: Queensland government pledges to restore dams in budget
items.description: The treasurer has also promised no cuts to public service, but won't commit to returning to surplus within the next four years.

items.title: Tony Modra's family 'extremely grateful' for support after crash
items.description: The family of AFL icon Tony Modra has released a statement thanking the community for the "overwhelming show of love" they have received since he was seriously injured in a crash last week.

items.title: Gus Lamont's grandmother denies involvement in disappearance
items.description: One of the grandmothers of missing four-year-old Gus Lamont says police have a theory that she buried her grandson after an accident — an allegation she describes as "ludicrous".

items.title: NSW corruption watchdog begins university governance probe
items.description: Allegations of favouritism, undeclared conflicts of interest and the misuse of official positions have dominated the opening day of the ICAC inquiry into governance at the University of Wollongong.

items.title: How gambling companies 'conduct psychological experiments' on their customers
items.description: Betting ads on TV have been front of mind in Canberra lately, but experts say we're overlooking the real firepower behind Australia's gambling industry: cutting-edge, hyper-personalised, online tech.

items.title: Two men arrested, denied bail after violent unrest in Central Australia
items.description: Two men have been arrested and denied bail after a violent disturbance in Yuendumu, in which multiple vehicles were allegedly set alight by armed offenders.
